label: Review of Codex's Get Inspired (#76), its quota and latency fixes (#79), a search/results split with configurable grid/flex and masonry gallery layouts (#81), then the toolchain move to Oxlint (#82) and Oxfmt (#85) that unblocked the TypeScript 7 upgrade (#86)
decisions: Get Inspired quota: a per-artist token bucket in FastAPI (burst 10, 1 per 2 s, per process); a provider 429 is a 503 outage, and 429 means only the artist's own limit; auto-search waits 600 ms and needs 3+ characters (Laurie)
The cache uses a psycopg pool; the bridge caches its Google ID token per instance; Met detail calls share a 10 s budget and a detail 429 fails the page as an outage (review)
Results stay on screen when a short edit is held back from auto-search, and the status names both searches, keywords and artist (Laurie, review)

Get Inspired splits into a container plus a form, a results hook, a toolbar and a results section; fascia gains a generic ImageGallery with grid or flex, masonry on or off, artist-facing controls (Laurie)
Masonry keeps DOM order equal to sort order: grid spans measured heights, flex uses order in a fixed-height column wrap; plain CSS columns rejected; masonry stays off without ResizeObserver (review)

Oxlint is the only linter, native rules first with a JS plugin only for gaps (ADR 0004); prefer-tag-over-role stays on and its three cases were fixed; the drop zone's drag handlers get one suppression; type parameters follow the two-character rule (Laurie)
Oxfmt replaces Biome as the formatter, matched to Biome's scope and import sorting, with format on save in VS Code (ADR 0005, Laurie)
TypeScript 7 adopted and the Dependabot major hold removed; the Stylelint config moves to stylelint.config.mjs so exceptions carry comments (Laurie)
Greptile is skipped on tooling PRs for speed (Laurie)
#80, the Cleveland Museum of Art provider, filed at P3, unparented (Laurie)

retro.went_well: The review of Codex's #76 focused on system-design gaps, not style, and each gap became a scoped fix. The search view was split into reusable pieces with four gallery layouts, and the design doc gained three sequence diagrams with code maps that Laurie can debug from. The Oxlint and Oxfmt migration, which Laurie estimated would take her several days, landed in an afternoon. Probing paid off: deliberate-violation files showed that the migrated config had dropped rules-of-hooks and that the Next.js JS plugin never fired without browser globals, both of which a clean lint run hid. Halving the grid spans proved the new masonry test can fail. Every outward write was read back.
retro.improve: Two defects in code I had just written escaped to review. A Met detail 429 was still caught as one missing painting, a few lines from where I had made provider 429s mean an outage. The held-back label described a search by `query || artist`, though a Met search can set both. Greptile caught both and both were fixed before merge, but the information was in hand when I wrote them.
retro.tooling_suggestion: For a tool migration, make a deliberate-violation probe the last step before calling the config done, and take rule and option lists from the tool's own CLI or schema. When a change gives an error a new meaning, grep the surrounding code for every place that catches it. In repos with stricter rules, check that the latest instruction explicitly says to commit or ship before running git commit.
